day01: hook
Day one of building my dream game. It's going to be magnificent.
idea1
Picture this. A pond. My pond. Full of the finest salmon money can buy.
idea2
Big, fat, gorgeous salmon. Do you have any idea what those are worth?
idea3
Bears are obsessed with salmon. They'll stand in a waterfall all day, waiting for one to jump in their mouth. Disgusting. Wonderful.
idea4
So the bears come to my pond, eat my fish, and pay me. Every single day. That's the game.
name
It's called The Bear Must Eat. Because they must. And I'll be charging.
squares
Right now everything is squares. I'm aware. Don't say it.
bear
The brown square is a bear. The orange one is me, obviously. The owner.
test
First test. All the bear has to do is walk to the pond. One job.
through
He walked straight through me. Through me! Do you know who I am?
water
And then he strolled across the water like he owns the place.
broken
He does not own the place. I own the place. It's broken, and I'm furious.
cta
Tomorrow, fish. Tell me which fish to add, and choose wisely.
day02: Day two. Fish. My precious, profitable fish.
They swim around, they look pretty, and they go up in value. Perfect employees.
And when two happy fish bump into each other, you get baby fish. Free inventory. I love nature.
Then I changed one tiny line of code, and look what they did.
Every single fish crammed into the corner. Why? I gave you an entire pond!
Apparently I forgot to normalize a vector. One vector. Humiliating.
Fixed it. Now the pond refills itself, and my fortune grows while I sleep.
Tomorrow, the customers arrive. Hungry ones.
day03: Day three. Five p.m. My favorite time of day.
The office lets out, and here they come...
every single bear, sprinting straight to my pond.
They cannonball in, grab a fish, and pay me five coins each.
This is it. This is the game. Money, flying straight into my pockets.
There are no fish left. None. They ate my entire pond.
And now they're just standing in the water, confused, like it's my fault.
It is not my fault. Balancing is tomorrow's problem.
day04: Day four. That orange square is an insult, and it's going.
That square is supposed to be me. Look at it. No hat, no style, nothing.
So I rebuilt myself, cube by cube, the way I deserve.
Top hat. Monocle. Gold chain. Filthy, disgustingly rich.
Then I gave myself far too many animations. Worth every second.
Goodbye, square. You will not be missed.
Now that is a pond owner.
day05: Day five. Let me introduce my customers.
This is office bear. He walks, he eats, he roars, and most importantly, he pays.
Then there's grandma bear, construction bear, and the CEO. The CEO tips.
Which one are you? Be honest. I can tell.
Now the brown squares finally become real bears.
Look at them. Cannonballing into my pond, eating my fish. Good. Keep eating.
The world is still squares, though. I'll deal with that tomorrow.
day06: Day six. My pond still looks like a spreadsheet.
So I drew the whole thing. Every single pixel.
Grass, trees, flowers, rocks, lily pads, and real fish worth real money.
Then I added day and night, so the bears can pay me around the clock.
Night is my favorite. Moonlight, fireflies, and nobody bothering me.
And remember, this is the exact same pond as day one.
day07: Day seven. You people have been leaving comments.
Someone asked for a banana fish. Fine. You'll get your banana fish.
I drew it pixel by pixel. Brown spots, and a little stem for a tail.
Then I put it in the game, as a very rare egg.
It's a banana. It's also a fish. And honestly? It's gorgeous.
And of course the bears eat it. They eat everything.
What should I add next? Comment it, and maybe I'll listen.
day08: Now you can build a whole restaurant around the pond.
Every piece lands with a little plonk and a puff of dust. Very satisfying.
Tables, a barbecue, a jukebox, and a big neon sign.
And at five p.m. they sit down, they eat, and they pay extra for the ambiance.
My little bear restaurant. I'm a genius.
day09: Day nine. The game worked, but it felt dead. Lifeless. Boring.
Comic words, squash and stretch, screen shake, coins, and way too many sound effects.
Now tell me which one you'd rather play.
day10: Day ten. I made a title screen worthy of me.
And yes, there's always a bear in the pond. Always.
Ten days ago, this was a brown square walking on water.
There's still so much to build. Should I keep going? Of course I should.
